correctness.rationale: Weak-* compactness ensures a maximizer; convex first variation forces a superlevel indicator of a nonconstant degree≤2 trigonometric polynomial, hence at most two arcs. Complementation reduces to alpha≤1/2. Exact Fourier integration for two arcs is strictly convex in center-separation cosine, reducing to touching or antipodal centers. At antipodal centers the objective is strictly convex in cos(a-b), reducing to a single arc or equal antipodal arcs. Endpoint comparison yields exactly q sin²(pi alpha)=p. Trace identity follows entrywise from weighted Gram matrix, including all gain cross terms. Boundaries alpha=1/2 and the phase-transition equality handled. Deterministic 21000 calculations complement, not replace, these analytic steps.

The known Abreu–Speckbacher theorem controls only the leading concentration eigenvalue for an unweighted analytic-polynomial subspace; by complementation it already yields unweighted three-dimensional trace-square extremality, which is explicitly excluded from novelty.
